label: Connectedness and Compactness
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 85 through 126 and turns two global questions into working tests. Connectedness asks whether a space admits a nontrivial clopen yes/no split, and compactness asks whether every open cover hides a finite subcover. Both ideas become practical tools once we specialize them to manifolds.

label: What Connectedness Forbids
notes: A space is connected when it cannot be cut into two disjoint nonempty open pieces. The working version is the clopen test: only the empty set and the whole space are simultaneously open and closed. Equivalently, every continuous map into a discrete two-point space must be constant on a connected domain.

label: Components and Discrete Probes
notes: Components are the maximal connected subsets, and they partition the space. A locally constant binary label corresponds to a continuous map into the two-point discrete space, so the number of such labels equals two raised to the component count. On a connected space only the two constant labels survive.

label: Continuous Images Stay Connected
notes: Continuous maps cannot manufacture a disconnection, so the image of a connected space is connected. Applied to a real-valued map on an interval this is exactly the intermediate value theorem: the image is an interval, so every intermediate value is attained. This single preservation theorem powers many later arguments.

label: Path Connectedness
notes: A path is a continuous map from the unit interval, so path connectedness is constructive: exhibit a path and two points share a path component. Convex Euclidean sets use straight segments, and punctured planes detour around the hole. Path connectedness always implies connectedness, but the converse can fail.

label: The Topologist's Sine Curve
notes: The closure of the oscillating graph together with the vertical segment is connected because closure preserves connectedness. Yet no path can leave the segment and reach the graph, since the oscillations compress without bound near the axis. This is the canonical example separating connectedness from path connectedness.

label: Local Connectedness on Manifolds
notes: Local connectedness and local path connectedness require small connected or path-connected neighborhoods at every point. Euclidean balls and half-balls satisfy both, so manifolds inherit them. In a locally path-connected space path components are open and coincide with components, which is why path construction proves connectedness inside the manifold category.

label: Compactness via Finite Subcovers
notes: A space is compact when every open cover admits a finite subcover, converting infinite local data into a finite certificate. The closed interval passes because any cover can be reduced to finitely many sets, while the open interval cover by intervals one over n through one fails: every finite piece misses a point near zero.

label: Heine-Borel and Products
notes: In Euclidean space compactness is exactly closed and bounded, the Heine-Borel theorem. Finite products of compact spaces are compact, the finite Tychonoff case, so closed boxes are compact and serve as the building blocks for the Heine-Borel characterization of compact subsets of n-dimensional Euclidean space.

label: Compact Images and Closed Maps
notes: Continuous images of compact spaces are compact, giving the extreme value theorem: a continuous real function on a compact space attains its maximum and minimum. Compact subsets of Hausdorff spaces are closed, so a continuous map from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is closed, the lemma behind quotient and embedding recognition.

label: Local Compactness and Proper Maps
notes: Local compactness asks for a basis of precompact neighborhoods, which manifold charts supply through balls and boundary half-balls whose closures are compact. A proper map pulls compact sets back to compact sets; the squaring map is proper while the sine map is not, since one fiber has an unbounded preimage escaping to infinity.

label: Recap and Invariants
notes: Connectedness is the absence of a nontrivial clopen decision, and path connectedness strengthens it but agrees with it on manifolds. Compactness turns infinite covers into finite certificates, survives continuous images and closed subsets, and through Heine-Borel, the closed-map lemma, and proper maps it drives the structural theorems of later chapters.
